headline: Duffy wants billions to replace contractor-run FAA network; Monday cancellations far lower
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Duffy wants billions to replace contractor-run FAA network; Monday cancellations far lower; Oil opens steady after Iran's claimed drone attack on a U.S. base in Bahrain; Carney: U.S. trade deal is closer, but not without a viable auto sector.

top.headline: Duffy wants billions to replace contractor-run FAA network; Monday cancellations far lower
top.what: U.S. airlines cancelled about 2,300 flights on Sunday, the third day of disruption after Friday's nationwide ground stop, but only about 144 were cancelled for Monday as of Sunday afternoon. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress for tens of billions of dollars to replace the contractor-run network behind the failure, and Democrats say most of the money already approved is unspent.
top.why: In the briefing on 1 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Oil opens steady after Iran's claimed drone attack on a U.S. base in Bahrain
top.what: Oil prices were little changed when trading resumed Sunday evening, with Brent crude just under US$96 a barrel, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they sent drones at a U.S. radar at a helicopter base in Bahrain. Bahrain says it shot the attacks down, and Iran's claims have not been independently verified.
top.why: In the briefing on 1 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Carney: U.S. trade deal is closer, but not without a viable auto sector
top.what: Speaking in Manila on Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said talks with Washington are making progress and a two-country deal is possible, but that Canada is not there yet. He said he will not sign any agreement that fails to keep Canada's auto industry viable.
top.why: In the briefing on 1 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ottawa and Ontario still seeking Stellantis CEO meeting as Brampton plant sale clock runs
top.what: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Saturday that his government is not satisfied with Stellantis's approach in Canada, and tied the future of the auto sector to trade talks with Washington. Ottawa and Ontario are still waiting to put their package to stop the Brampton plant sale to global chief executive Antonio Filosa.
top.why: In the briefing on 1 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada's October inflation report lands Monday at 8:30 a.m., with forecasts from 3.0% to 3.3%
top.what: Statistics Canada reports October consumer prices on Monday, the last inflation reading before the Bank of Canada's Dec. 9 rate decision. Economists expect the annual rate to stay close to September's 3.1%, but disagree on whether high energy costs are spreading to other prices.
top.why: In the briefing on 1 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Peltola claims victory in Alaska; race still uncalled ahead of Wednesday's ranked-choice count
top.what: Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign has declared victory in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, where she holds about 49.9% of first-choice votes to Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan's 46%. The Associated Press has not called the race, and a ranked-choice tabulation is set for Wednesday if no one tops 50%.

top.headline: Ontario Catholic teachers vote 98 per cent in favour of strike mandate
top.what: The union representing Catholic teachers says educators are dealing with chronic classroom underfunding by the Ford government.
